ACM @ RCC

Fall 2026 · Thursday, November 19

What should we build next semester?

Today we pick projects for spring, built by people in this room. You leave with a group and a first step.

Nobody commits to anything final today. December 3 is for scoping the picks, and December 10 is for locking teams.

Before the meeting: sticky notes in two colors, markers, 3 dot stickers per person, and a clear whiteboard. Full plan: semesters/2026-fall/meetings/2026-11-19-plan.md.

Here's how the hour goes.

Today

How the hour goes

  1. Look back at what we did this fallPick out what you'd keep building
  2. Write your ideas on sticky notesOne idea per note
  3. Group the notes, then vote3 dots each
  4. Sign up with a groupAnswer 4 questions together

Fills in on its own. One press shows the rest. The next press moves on.

The bar on the right is the hour to scale. Sign-up gets the most time because that's where groups actually form.

First, what we did this fall.

What we did this fall

  1. Oct 1Instagram's feed, Reels ranking, and who to follow
  2. Oct 8 and 15Arduino servo, button, and transistor fan
  3. Oct 29ICPC practice, or the parking garage gate
  4. Nov 7ICPC regional, hosted at RCC

Words only on purpose: this is a dated list, and every line is a meeting people sat through. For each line, ask the room who wanted to keep going on it, and write those topics on the whiteboard.

Seeds if the room is quiet. Oct 1: build a small feed or follow-suggestion engine on made-up users. Oct 8 and 15: bigger builds with the same parts. Oct 29: a full garage that counts cars in and out and shows open spots. Nov 7: a spring practice league for the next regional.

Not on the slide: Sep 24 (tech roles activity and sample ICPC problems), Nov 5 and Nov 12 [TBD: add if worth mentioning], and Cal Hacks [TBD: add only if the club went as ACM].

So which one do you want to keep building?

Hands up

Which of these would you keep building?

Say it out loud. It goes on the board as a starting point for your notes.

Two or three minutes. Write each answer on the whiteboard in a few words. These are seeds; people can still write anything on their sticky notes.

Here's hardware we own that nobody has used yet.

Parts nobody has used yet

  • 6 ESP-32 boards

    Wi-Fi, so a build can put data on a web page

    Photo: Edwiyanto, CC BY-SA 4.0
  • 2 Mega 2560 boards

    Lots more pins than the UNO

    Photo: Goga504, CC BY-SA 4.0
  • Stepper motors

    Turn an exact amount, to move a part to a set spot

From semesters/2026-fall/lab-inventory.md: 6 ESP-32 boards, 2 Mega 2560 boards, 3 UNO R4 WiFi, 1 L298N motor driver, and 5 extra stepper sets plus one in each Elegoo kit. None of these have been in a lab yet. A project that uses them needs no new purchase.

Example: the elevator challenge in the microcontroller lab repo could run on steppers.

Now write your own ideas.

On your own · 8 minutes

Write your ideas

One idea per sticky note, as many as you want. Ideas from today's board count.

Press T. Quiet writing, no discussion yet. An idea can be one line, like "a garage that shows open spots".

Time's up. Now we share them.

Together · 12 minutes

Share and group

  1. Read your notes out loudOne person at a time
  2. Stick each one on the board
  3. Same idea? Put them together
  4. Name each groupOne sentence about what gets built

Run it at the whiteboard. When two notes are the same idea, stack them. A group's name says what gets built, like "a garage sign that shows open spots", not a topic like "hardware".

Now everyone votes.

Vote · 5 minutes

You get 3 dots. Put them on what you'd actually work on

You can put more than one dot on the same group.

Hand out 3 dot stickers per person. The point is to find which groups have people behind them, so ask people to vote for what they would spend spring on, not what sounds cool.

The groups with the most dots sign up next.

Each group answers

Sign up with a group

  1. What do you want to build?One sentence
  2. Who's in?First names
  3. What would you try first?Something you could do before February
  4. What would you need?Parts, a skill, a person, or time

Every group with 2 or more dots-and-people stands together. One person per group writes the answers on a sheet. Nobody needs to know question 4 yet.

"Before February" because spring classes start February 16, 2027.

You have until 2:22.

Group time · until 2:22

Answer the 4 questions

One person writes. Then each group reads its answers to the room.

Press T. The clock counts down to 2:22, so starting late is fine. Walk between groups. Then each group gets 30 seconds to read its answers.
